sofia: Quick heads-up — noticed a p99 spike on streaming chat after we bumped microbatch size 4->8 on pool-a.
sofia: Model: gpt-medium-16k, route: chat/streaming, affected nodes: rtx-pool-a.{1..3}  :thinking_face:
amr: Ugh. Any traces/metrics? p50/p95/p99 numbers?
sofia: p50 ~ 35ms, p95 ~ 120ms, p99 jumped from 240ms -> 470ms. KV cache hit rate dropped ~3x in the same window.
infra-bot: canary-deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-18T09:10:23 to pool-a completed (no immediate errors)
jay: Did the runtime change kernel selection around that time? Kernel sampler logs might show fallback to a less efficient matmul kernel when mbsize crosses threshold.
sofia: I pulled a kernel sampler trace. It shows a fallback to the generic matmul path for the last tokens when MB>=6. Snippet:
```
kernel_sampler: chosen_kernel=matmul_generic, reason=kvcache_warmup_miss, median_latency=12.3ms
handshake: wait=8.7ms
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.31 -> 0.92 (post-change)
```
maya: That matches a hypothesis: increasing MB forces different kernel tiling and increases contention on KV-prefetch, which amplifies tail latencies for streaming (handshake-sensitive). Non-streaming completions tolerate batching cost better.
amr: Good call. We should measure both streaming and sync completions across MB sizes [2,4,6,8] and record p50/p95/p99 + kv_hit_rate + handshake_time.
sofia: Proposed perf-run command (quick harness):
```
./perf_runner --model gpt-medium-16k --pool pool-a --mode streaming --mbsize 4 --duration 600 --trace kv,handshake,latency --out /tmp/run.json
```
jay: Add kernel-chooser debug flag too: `--kernel-debug` so we get exact fallback reasons.
maya: Experiment plan: run 1h per config (streaming vs non-streaming) for mbsize [2,4,6,8], collect kv_hit, handshake ms, kernel ids. Compare p99 and compute tail amplification factor = p99_stream/p99_nonstream.
sofia: I'll kick off runs tonight on a small canary subset (2 nodes) and post summaries in the morning. If we see MB>=6 consistently bad for streaming, propose a soft cap for streaming routes to mb<=4 + a runtime heuristic that prefers kernels with lower handshake when kvcache miss rate > 0.2.
amr: Also consider adaptive-prefetch: if kvcache miss rate rises we can increase prefetch depth or switch to pre-warm handshake path. Could be cheaper than capping mb.
jay: Two quick checks: 1) profile L2 contention on those nodes, 2) check if quantized int8 kernels have different behavior for small vs large MB. I've seen int8 path avoid some matmul_generic.
sofia: Agreed. For the roll criteria: if p99 improves by >=30% on streaming without >5% throughput loss, uncap MB ramp; else enforce cap and follow up with prefetch prototype.
maya: tagging perf-dashboard owners for a new panel: kv_hit_rate, handshake_ms, kernel_id, mbsize, route_type -> so we can correlate quickly.
sofia: thanks — will post raw traces + a summary thread after runs. :white_check_mark:
